question: True or false: most cancer clusters investigated by US health agencies turned out to have an environmental cause?
answer: False. A 2012 review of 428 US investigations over two decades confirmed a real excess of cancer in 72, and almost never found a cause. With thousands of towns and dozens of cancer types, some neighbourhoods will show a cluster by chance alone, and those are the ones people notice and report.
move: Ask how many places could have produced the pattern before suspecting this one.
ask: When bad things bunch up around me, have I asked how often such a bunch happens by chance?
trap: True, since a cluster feels too striking to be chance.
source: Goodman et al., Critical Reviews in Toxicology, 2012
reference: Goodman, Naiman, Goodman & LaKind, Cancer clusters in the USA: what do the last twenty years of state and federal investigations tell us?, Critical Reviews in Toxicology 42:474–490, 2012
